h: Plane Spotting, Motorbikes and a Spin on the Ice
p: Hobs Moat Road sits on the east side of Solihull, close to Birmingham Airport and the NEC, which opens up a few fun extras for your day. The National Motorcycle Museum is just a short drive away and is a real treat for anyone who loves two wheels, with a huge collection of British bikes under one roof. If you're visiting for an event at the NEC, a quick skate can be a lively way to unwind before or after.

Into the centre of Solihull and you've got Touchwood for shopping and places to eat, plus the leafy streets around the town centre for a gentle wander. Malvern and Brueton Parks are a pleasant green space close to the centre, with lakes and walking paths for a breather.

Back on the ice, a few quick tips. Wear gloves, a warm layer and trousers rather than shorts or skirts. Make sure your skate laces are tight around the ankles for support. Beginners should keep their knees bent and take small steps, and if you feel yourself going, sit down sideways rather than falling backwards.

If you've got kids in tow, a skating aid is worth asking about for the smallest skaters. It gives them something to lean on and frees your hands up so you can actually enjoy the session rather than bending double the whole time. Everyone's a winner.
